text: Given two bound configs from two different real Keeper accounts, When each is used to call keeper_list_secrets / keeper_get_secret, Then each only ever sees its own account's records and folders -- never the other's
steps: Obtain two bound KSM configs from two separate real Keeper Secrets Manager accounts (needs a real vendor account; cannot be faked -- Keeper's account/vault separation is enforced server-side)
Call keeper_list_secrets and keeper_get_secret with config A, record the returned UIDs/titles
Call the same tools with config B, record the returned UIDs/titles
expect: The two result sets never overlap except by true coincidence of UID values (which KSM UIDs do not collide on in practice); config A never returns a record/folder that only exists in account B's vault and vice versa
evidence: Not executed: no real Keeper Secrets Manager account/vault was available to this pipeline at build time (2026-11-02). Not a delivery blocker per vendor-mcp-development SOP ("no test account is not a blocker"). Isolation at the code level (TC9) is covered and passing; this case needs a real second data source to confirm end to end.

text: Given a real bound KSM config produced by redeeming a one-time token once outside this service, When the agent runs create -> get -> update -> delete on a scratch secret end to end, Then every step succeeds against the live Keeper cloud API, confirming the bound config actually authenticates in production conditions
steps: In a real Keeper Vault, create an Application + Client Device, generate a One-Time Access Token, and redeem it once via Keeper's own tooling (e.g. Keeper Commander or the SDK's bootstrap) to obtain the bound config
Base64-encode the resulting configuration and send it as X-Keeper-Config on tools/call keeper_create_secret to create a scratch login record in a test folder
Call keeper_get_secret with the returned uid and confirm the fields match what was created
Call keeper_update_secret to change one field, then keeper_get_secret again to confirm the change
Call keeper_delete_secret with that uid and confirm it is gone from a subsequent keeper_list_secrets
expect: Every step returns a successful tool result; no step requires redeeming a second one-time token (confirming the bound config, not the token, is what is reused per call)
evidence: Not executed: no real Keeper Secrets Manager account/vault was available to this pipeline at build time (2026-11-02). Not a delivery blocker per vendor-mcp-development SOP. Each step's logic is covered individually by TC3/TC5/TC6/TC7 (mocked SDK); this case needs a live vault to confirm the sequence end to end against the real Keeper cloud API.
